name: DailyPay VDP
policy:
## **Introduction**
At DailyPay, we are dedicated to delivering secure products and services. We value the input of independent security researchers and the broader community in helping us maintain a secure technological landscape.

If you believe you've identified a potential security vulnerability within DailyPay's systems, we want to hear from you. 

> TIP: **Exceptional reports don't just help us stay safe, they may also warrant an invite to our private, paid Bug Bounty program!**

---

## **Response Targets**
We make a best effort to meet the following response timelines for researchers:

| Type of Response | Target (Business Days) |
| :--- | :--- |
| **First Response** | 2 Days |
| **Time to Triage** | 8 Days |
| **Time to Resolution** | Varies by severity and complexity |

---

## **Program Rules & Disclosure**
To remain in good standing, we ask that you adhere to the following:

* **Confidentiality:** Do not discuss vulnerabilities (including resolved ones) outside this program without express written consent.
* **Standard Guidelines:** Follow the [HackerOne Disclosure Guidelines](https://www.hackerone.com/disclosure-guidelines).
* **Report Quality:** Submit one vulnerability per report (unless chaining for impact). Reports must include clear, reproducible steps.
* **Duplicates:** Only the first reproducible report of a vulnerability will be triaged.
* **Good Faith Effort:** Make a good faith effort to avoid privacy violations, data destruction, or service degradation. Only interact with accounts you own.
* **Prohibited:** Social engineering (phishing, vishing, etc.) against DailyPay employees or users is strictly forbidden.
* **Auto-Generated Client SDKs:** DailyPay publishes client SDKs generated by third-party tooling (Speakeasy). These codebases are not written or directly maintained by DailyPay. All valid findings will be classed as **Informational Only**. Issues will be escalated to the third-party vendor where applicable.

> SDK repos covered by this rule:
> - dailypay-typescript-sdk
> - dailypay-go-sdk
> - dailypay-dotnet8-sdk
> - dailypay-dotnet9-sdk

---

## **Scope & Identification**
Testing is **strictly limited** to assets listed as "In-Scope." Anything not listed is considered Out-of-Scope. If you discover a vulnerability in an unlisted asset, please contact `support@hackerone.com` before submitting.

### **Mandatory Testing Header**
To ensure our SOC doesn't block your activity, all manual and automated testing tools **must** include the following HTTP header:
`X-HackerOne-DailyPay-Research: [Your H1 Username]`

---

## **Before You Submit**

Please confirm all of the following before submitting a report:

- [ ] My vulnerability affects **production systems** (not test, dev, or staging)
- [ ] I have a **working proof of concept**
- [ ] I can demonstrate **actual security impact** (not just theoretical)
- [ ] My attack scenario is **realistic** (not dependent on extensive social engineering)
- [ ] This is not just a missing security header or best practice violation
- [ ] The vulnerability is not in an out-of-scope asset listed below

Reports that do not meet these criteria will be marked as N/A or Informational without further review.

---

## **What Makes a Strong Report**

To be considered a high-quality submission, your report should demonstrate **all three** of the following:

**1. Working Proof of Concept**
Demonstrate the vulnerability against our production systems with step-by-step reproduction instructions, evidence (screenshots, HTTP requests/responses, or video), and a clear explanation of the security impact. Reports lacking an adequate PoC will be marked as N/A or Informative.

**2. Clear Security Impact**
Your report should show at least one of the following:
- Unauthorized access to data or functionality
- Authentication or authorization bypass
- Remote code execution
- Data exfiltration or modification by unauthorized parties
- Financial loss through attacker-controlled actions

We do not accept: data validation issues without security consequences, business logic flaws that only affect operational reliability, compliance violations without a demonstrated exploitation path, or issues that only cause service degradation or incorrect processing.

**3. Realistic Attack Scenario**
Exploits requiring extensive user interaction will be considered lower severity or informative. This includes scenarios requiring the victim to take multiple suspicious actions, install malicious software, or visit attacker-controlled sites in ways that a typical security-aware user would recognize as suspicious.

> **Note:** Exceptional submissions demonstrating significant, well-documented impact are most likely to result in an invitation to our private Bug Bounty program.

---

## **Out-of-Scope Vulnerabilities**

When reporting, please focus on **exploitability** and **security impact**. The following issues are generally considered out of scope:

### Third-Party & Open Source Libraries

We do not accept reports for known CVEs in third-party libraries unless you demonstrate:
* The vulnerable version is running in our production environment
* Our implementation uses the vulnerable functionality
* You have a working exploit in our specific production context

Vulnerabilities in open-source projects we depend on will not be accepted without proof they are exploitable in our deployed implementation.

### Non-Production & Test Assets

The following are explicitly out of scope:
* Test repositories, take-home assignments, and example code
* Development, staging, or QA environments (unless explicitly listed as in scope)
* Internal tools not accessible to end users
* GitHub repositories that do not power production services
* Archived repositories (no longer maintained)

### Web & General Policy

* **CSRF/Clickjacking:** On pages with no sensitive actions or unauthenticated forms.
* **Configuration:** Missing best practices in SSL/TLS, CSP, or HTTP headers (e.g., HttpOnly, Secure flags) without a demonstrated exploit.
* **Email:** Missing SPF/DKIM/DMARC records or general email best practices.
* **Redirects:** Open redirects unless a significant security impact is demonstrated.
* **Information Disclosure:** Software version disclosure, banner identification, stack traces, or descriptive error messages.
* **Rate Limiting:** On non-authentication endpoints.
* **CORS misconfiguration** without an exploitation scenario.
* **Broken link hijacking** issues.
* **Improper logout functionality** and improper session timeout.
* **Disclosure of IP addresses.**
* **User enumeration** without a demonstrated account takeover path.
* **Missing security headers** (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.) without a demonstrated exploit.

### Technical Limitations

* **User Interaction:** Issues requiring unlikely or "perfect world" user interaction (e.g., Tabnabbing).
* **Access:** Attacks requiring MITM or physical access to a user's device.
* **Environment:** Debug info or partial source code disclosure in development/staging environments.
* **Known Vulnerabilities:** Vulnerabilities in outdated browsers (less than 2 stable versions behind), "Zero-day" vulnerabilities patched within the last 30 days, or previously known vulnerable libraries without a working Proof of Concept.
* **Archived Repositories:** Findings in archived repositories will not be accepted as these are no longer maintained.
* **Theoretical Issues:** Vulnerabilities that are not exploitable or cannot be demonstrated as exploitable against production systems.

### Low Impact / Automated

* **CSV Injection:** Without a demonstrated vulnerability.
* **Scanner Reports:** Raw, unvalidated output from automated tools.
* **Public Data:** Publicly known Google API keys, leaked credentials from dark web sources, or breach lists.
* **WordPress:** Issues on unauthenticated endpoints of WordPress sites or XMLRPC.
* **Operational/Business Logic Issues:** Input validation failures, retry logic flaws, or processing errors that do not create an attacker-controlled security impact.

### Mobile Specific

* Lack of SSL Pinning or Jailbreak detection.

---

Thank you for helping keep DailyPay and our users safe!
